text:
Valeri Nichushkin spent 404 games in Colorado, won a Stanley Cup there in 2022, and is 22 games into life with the Blue Jackets. It hasn't clicked at the net. He has two goals and 11 points, only 31 shots, and 3.0 expected goals of his own, a sharp drop for a winger who used to live around the crease.

Part of that is the company. In Colorado he played beside some of the league's best, and Evolving-Hockey still had him 47th among forwards in wins above replacement last season. In Columbus the line around him is different, and the Blue Jackets take 49% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on, only 1.5 points better than without him. He still does the quiet work: 39 hits, and he exits the zone with possession 64% of the time in Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking. His point rate sits a little below his talent range. Our range projects 41 to 62 points. The fix, if there is one, is getting him back to the net front.
